Imported corpus's contradiction #3 (multi-agent coordination vs measurable coordination overhead) supports keeping single-agent as the default and multi-agent orchestration opt-in, not a default hierarchy. Consistent with this repository's own minimal-core bias; not yet cross-checked against the existing locked architecture per the corpus's own caveat that candidate deletions/changes need that comparison first.

The imported corpus proposes 6 ADR-CANDIDATEs (separate Runtime from Agent semantics; formalize State/Memory/Context/Knowledge/Evidence/Transcript; introduce ContextBroker; mandatory action-boundary policy for dangerous capabilities; opt-in multi-agent orchestration; semantic adapter policy for external frameworks) and 10 proposed benchmarks. None have been compared against the existing locked architecture (docs/architecture/PACKAGE-MAP.md, existing ADRs) or cross-checked against this session's own installment 1-3 findings yet - that reconciliation is future work, not performed as part of this import.

Strands/smolagents minimal model-driven loops vs Haystack/Llama Agents/Microsoft-successor explicit workflows for durable control - argues for a small kernel with workflow as an optional, not mandatory, layer. Overlaps with and reinforces the LangGraph/Mastra installment 3 finding that workflow orchestration is core-vs-attached varies by framework family. Imported claim, DOCUMENTED_NOT_REPRODUCED - not independently re-verified this session.

Directly reinforces batch 1's adopt-durable-state-distinct-from-memory candidate - now evidenced independently by strands-agents, smolagents, llama-index, haystack AND microsoft-agent-framework (5 sources total across both batches plus this session's own MAF research). Two independent imported corpora converging on the same six-way split is stronger evidence than either alone. Imported claim, DOCUMENTED_NOT_REPRODUCED - not independently re-verified this session.

Reinforces batch 1's reject-llm-only-security-judgement finding from OpenHands - capability-scoped, deterministic tool security rather than relying on model judgement. Imported claim, DOCUMENTED_NOT_REPRODUCED - not independently re-verified this session.

Proposes defining local-first as a capability contract (CloudAccount=optional, Network=denyable, ModelProvider=local/remote interchangeable, Storage=filesystem/sqlite/embedded selectable, Tools=explicit capability grants, Observability=local sink required, Evaluation=runnable offline) rather than a single LOCAL_NATIVE/CLOUD_ONLY label - see research/comparison/NEXT-WAVE-RUNTIME-LOCAL-FIRST.md. Worth reconciling against this repository's own local-first scorecard enum in a future installment, not silently adopted as the replacement here. Imported claim, DOCUMENTED_NOT_REPRODUCED - not independently re-verified this session.

DSPy's optimization capability (prompt/program compilation) is valuable but should live outside the runtime kernel as a separate OptimizationPort, distinct from an EvaluationPort - avoids coupling evaluation/training into the core runtime interfaces. See research/frameworks/dspy/overview.md. Imported claim, DOCUMENTED_NOT_REPRODUCED - not independently re-verified this session.

Proposes an Operation ID + UNKNOWN_OUTCOME model for side effects that time out with unknown remote state - production agents need reconciliation, not just success/failure. No cited evidence sources in the source corpus's own spec-delta.json (SPEC-005), unlike the other 5 candidates - flagged as the weakest-evidenced of the 6, not silently treated as equally supported. Imported claim, DOCUMENTED_NOT_REPRODUCED - not independently re-verified this session.

Batch 2's own spec-delta.json proposes 6 SPEC changes (State/Memory/Context/Knowledge/Evidence/Transcript separation; WorkspaceContract+SandboxContract; optional DurableWorkflow layer; EvaluationPort; Operation ID+UNKNOWN_OUTCOME side-effect state; OptimizationPort outside kernel) and gap-delta.json proposes 8 prioritized gaps (durable execution semantics, side-effect reconciliation, workspace security, multi-agent economics, context compression quality, offline evaluation, MCP trust, schema/version migration - all P0/P1/P2 tagged). None reconciled against the existing locked architecture or against batch 1's own 6 ADR-CANDIDATEs for overlap/redundancy yet - both imported corpora's architectural proposals need a single reconciliation pass before any of them move past CANDIDATE.

A third user-supplied corpus (distinct in kind from the two framework-research imports - a proposed operational protocol for this repository's OWN git/PR/CI/deploy lifecycle, not research about external frameworks) is stored at docs/operations/post-commit-ops/. It proposes a 25-state lifecycle state machine, merge/release gates, an AI code-review protocol, CI failure/verification runbooks, security gates, a no-bypass policy, an evidence-ledger contract, recovery/rollback protocols, and machine-readable agent-contract/lifecycle JSON. It is NOT wired into AGENTS.md (the canonical operating contract) or CI - adopting any part of it requires an explicit ADR, same as any other architectural/governance decision, per this repository's own anti-drift rule. docs/ is outside okf.json's validated scopes, so this bundle was not okf-conformance-checked by CI, but one systematic non-conformance (verified: documented, a bare string where OKF requires a mapping) was fixed anyway for consistency.

The post-commit-ops bundle's UNKNOWN_OUTCOME/RECONCILING states (for merges, deployments, and any side effect with an ambiguous remote result) independently converge with research corpus batch 2's ADR-CANDIDATE-006 (Operation ID + UNKNOWN_OUTCOME side-effect model, decisions.json id adr-candidate-006-durable-side-effect-reconciliation) - two separately-supplied corpora, one about external framework patterns and one about this repository's own git/CI/deploy operations, both landing on 'never blindly retry an operation whose side effect has an unknown outcome, reconcile actual state first' as a hard rule. Worth treating as reinforcing evidence when Phase 4/7 persistence work and any future CI/release automation are designed, not yet adopted as an ADR.

A cross-corpus consolidation graph was built at the user's request, covering all 6 research/governance corpora integrated so far (this session's own live research + batch1 + batch2 + batch3/current-wave + post-commit-ops + wave1). It is explicitly a SUPPLEMENTARY cross-reference/audit layer, not a replacement for this file or gaps.json or the OKF-frontmatter research/ markdown tree, which remain the authoritative, CI-validated record per ADR-0007. Built this way rather than replacing the existing system because the new LabLaunchPad.ResearchCanonical schema is a different, non-OKF-conformant shape, and silently swapping the knowledge system's architecture was judged an undiscussed change this repository's own rules guard against. Its main net-new contribution: cross-corpus contradiction/version-drift detection (see CTR-A2A-VERSION, resolved) and a first delete_test pass over 25 candidate architecture boundaries, surfacing 3 evidenced-but-unplanned ADD_CANDIDATE boundaries (WorkspaceEngine, SandboxEngine, SideEffectEngine) not previously named as a set in gaps.json.
